subject.title: [Bug]: Concurrent allow-always approvals silently lose allowlist entries (last-write-wins race in exec-approvals.json)

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix path for exec approval stale writes, or sponsor a narrower allow-always-only fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug affects command-execution approval state and overlaps an open security-sensitive PR with proof and merge-risk blockers, so automation should not start a new repair branch without maintainer direction.

options.title: Adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix
options.body: Use the broader locked/CAS approval mutation direction, refreshed on current main and cleared through security and real-behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow allow-always fix
options.body: Limit the repair to concurrent allow-always persistence if maintainers want to defer the broader node/macOS stale-writeback fix.

options.title: Wait for the security PR track
options.body: Keep this issue open while the node stale-writeback security PR establishes the shared persistence primitive first.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace the shared guarded-write fix
recommendation.body: Use the broader locked/CAS approval mutation direction, refreshed on current main and cleared through security and real-behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on exec approval persistence and policy-layer changes touching this boundary.
